author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Dolphin routes real Balance Boards to the correct Android slot
summary: Android's DolphinBar scanner now distinguishes a Wii Balance Board from an ordinary remote, matching the device routing already used on desktop platforms.
heroAlt: Source evidence from Dolphin pull request #14673: Android: Route DolphinBar Balance Board to the Balance Board slot

sourceLabels.dolphin-pr-14673: Android: Route DolphinBar Balance Board to the Balance Board slot

blocks.text: A connected board was classified as Player 1's remote

The Android scanner accepted every device arriving through a Mayflash DolphinBar into its Wii Remote result list. A comment already noted that balance boards were not differentiated. The transport worked and the board could sync, but Dolphin assigned it to a normal remote slot. Wii Fit and Wii Fit Plus ask specifically for the Balance Board device, so they continued showing a sync prompt despite successful Bluetooth communication.
Device identity now selects the result collection

Pull request #14673 uses the existing Wiimote::IsBalanceBoard check while enumerating DolphinBar devices. A positive result is moved into balance_boards; every other device follows the original wii_remotes path. This mirrors Linux and Windows scanner behavior and reuses classification that the Wiimote object already knows, rather than adding Android-only USB identifiers or a title-specific workaround.
Hardware testing covered board and remote behavior together

The reported test used an official RVL-WBC-01 board, a Mayflash DolphinBar in Mode 4, and an Android 13 handheld. With Balance Board source set to Real Balance Board and continuous scanning enabled, Wii Fit Plus recognized and used the device after the change. A standard Wii Remote connected through the same bar still occupied a remote slot, providing the important negative control for the new branch.
Multiple-device and reconnect sequences complete the matrix

Test cold boot and hot-plug with one board, one remote, both together in each synchronization order, and reconnect after sleep or USB permission renewal. Verify board input values, calibration, disconnect cleanup, continuous scan, and slot persistence across activity recreation. Add a fake or unsupported HID device to ensure IsBalanceBoard does not misclassify it. Desktop scanner behavior should remain untouched, and Android logs should clearly identify which collection received each device.
Transport detection only answers what is connected; Wii software also needs Dolphin to route that physical device into the semantic slot it requested.
